title: Android Kotlin Flows
description: Beginner-to-advanced reference for building, transforming, sharing, lifecycle-aware collection, Room and Paging integration, debugging, and testing Kotlin Flow streams in Android applications.

sections.title: Flow Mental Model
sections.description: Understand what a Flow represents before choosing builders or operators.

subtopics.title: Cold Streams & Collection
subtopics.description: A Flow describes asynchronous values. A cold Flow runs its upstream block independently for every collector and does no work until collected.

annotations.text: Creates a cold Flow description; the body is suspendable.
Terminal operator starts upstream work and suspends until completion.

callouts.title: Flow Is Sequential by Default
callouts.text: Each operator and collector normally executes sequentially in the collecting coroutine. Concurrency appears only when an operator such as buffer, flatMapMerge, shareIn, or a separate coroutine introduces it.

callouts.title: Nothing Happens Without Collection
callouts.text: Creating a cold Flow does not start requests, database reads, or timers. Ensure the intended owner collects it or converts it to a deliberately scoped hot stream.

subtopics.title: Choose Suspend, Flow, StateFlow, or SharedFlow
subtopics.description: Use a suspend function for one result, Flow for a changing stream, StateFlow for observable current state, and SharedFlow for broadcast values when state semantics do not fit.

table.title: Asynchronous API Selection
rows: Only if an operator adds it
Fan out values to multiple active collectors
Buffered until received, not replayed to all

callouts.title: Events Versus State
callouts.text: Do not represent durable UI facts as one-time events. If losing a value during configuration change would produce an incorrect screen, model it as state and acknowledge it through state transitions.

sections.title: Building Flows
sections.description: Create streams from suspend code, callbacks, collections, and existing state.

subtopics.title: flow, flowOf, asFlow & channelFlow
subtopics.description: Select the smallest builder that matches the producer. Use flow for sequential emissions and channelFlow when child coroutines must emit concurrently.

tabs.label: Common Builders
Concurrent Producer

callouts.title: Emission Context Invariant
callouts.text: Do not launch another coroutine or use withContext to call emit inside flow. Use flowOn to move upstream work, or channelFlow/send for concurrent producers.

subtopics.title: Convert Callback APIs with callbackFlow
subtopics.description: Bridge multi-shot listener APIs into a cold Flow and always unregister the callback when collection stops.

annotations.text: Non-suspending send suitable for callback threads; inspect failure if loss matters.
Keeps the channel open and performs mandatory cleanup on cancellation.

callouts.title: Cleanup Is Not Optional
callouts.text: Missing awaitClose can leak listeners. Registration may also throw; handle permission and platform failures according to the API contract.

sections.title: Transforming & Combining Streams
sections.description: Build readable pipelines and make cancellation semantics explicit.

subtopics.title: map, filter, transform & onEach
subtopics.description: Intermediate operators return a new cold Flow; they do not start collection.

callouts.title: Keep onEach Non-Blocking
callouts.text: onEach is useful for logging and small side effects, but it remains part of the sequential pipeline. Long work delays downstream collection.

subtopics.title: mapLatest & flatMap Families
subtopics.description: Choose based on whether new input cancels, queues, or runs alongside previous work.

tabs.label: Latest Search
Operator Semantics
tabs.code:
flatMapConcat: finish each inner Flow in order
flatMapMerge: collect inner Flows concurrently (bounded concurrency)
flatMapLatest: cancel the previous inner Flow when new input arrives
mapLatest/collectLatest: cancel only the previous transform/collector body

callouts.title: Cancellation Must Be Safe
callouts.text: Latest operators cancel superseded work. Do not use them for operations that must commit exactly once unless the operation is transaction-safe or runs in an appropriate longer-lived scope.

subtopics.title: combine, zip & merge
subtopics.description: combine emits whenever either source changes after both have emitted; zip pairs by position; merge forwards values as they arrive.

codeBlocks.code:
val uiState: Flow<SearchUiState> = combine(
    repository.results,
    preferences.filters,
    connectivity.status
) { results, filters, online ->
    SearchUiState(results.apply(filters), online)
}

annotations.text: Recomputes from the latest value of every input after all inputs emit once.

callouts.title: Initial Emissions Matter
callouts.text: combine cannot emit until every input has emitted. StateFlow inputs avoid an unexpected blank period because each has an initial value.

sections.title: Context, Buffering & Failure
sections.description: Control where work runs, how slow collectors affect producers, and where exceptions are handled.

subtopics.title: flowOn, buffer & conflate
subtopics.description: flowOn changes the context of upstream operators. buffer lets producer and collector overlap. conflate retains only the newest value for a slow collector.

codeBlocks.code:
fun thumbnails(): Flow<Bitmap> = imageIds()
    .map { id -> decodeThumbnail(id) }
    .flowOn(dispatchers.default) // map and imageIds upstream
    .buffer(capacity = 8)        // bounded producer/consumer overlap

thumbnails().collectLatest(::render)

callouts.title: Preserve Main Safety
callouts.text: Prefer making repositories and data sources main-safe internally. flowOn affects only upstream; it does not move the downstream collector.

callouts.title: Loss Policy Is Product Behavior
callouts.text: conflate, collectLatest, and drop overflow policies intentionally skip work or values. Use them for replaceable state or rendering, never silently for payments, audit events, or ordered writes.

subtopics.title: catch, retryWhen & onCompletion
subtopics.description: catch sees upstream exceptions but not failures thrown later in the collector. CancellationException must remain cancellation.

callouts.title: Catch Near the Recoverable Boundary
callouts.text: Place catch after the operations whose failures can be converted into a domain value. Avoid swallowing programmer errors with a broad Throwable fallback.

sections.title: StateFlow, SharedFlow & Sharing
sections.description: Model observable state and share expensive upstream work with deliberate lifetime rules.

subtopics.title: StateFlow as an Immutable State API
subtopics.description: StateFlow is hot, always has a current value, replays that value to new collectors, and conflates updates using equality.

callouts.title: Atomic Updates
callouts.text: Use update or compareAndSet when the next value depends on the current value; direct read-modify-write can lose concurrent changes.

callouts.title: Immutable Values
callouts.text: Mutating a list or object already stored in StateFlow may not emit because equality has not changed. Publish a new immutable value.

subtopics.title: stateIn, shareIn & SharingStarted
subtopics.description: Convert a cold Flow to a shared hot stream in a scope that lives exactly as long as the shared resource should live.

codeBlocks.code:
val uiState: StateFlow<FeedUiState> = repository.observeFeed()
    .map<List<Article>, FeedUiState> { FeedUiState.Ready(it) }
    .stateIn(
        scope = viewModelScope,
        started = SharingStarted.WhileSubscribed(5_000),
        initialValue = FeedUiState.Loading
    )

val sharedUpdates: SharedFlow<Update> = expensiveUpdates.shareIn(
    scope = applicationScope,
    started = SharingStarted.WhileSubscribed(),
    replay = 1
)

callouts.title: Scope Defines Lifetime
callouts.text: A scope that is too short repeatedly restarts work; one that is too long retains resources. WhileSubscribed with a small timeout avoids churn during brief configuration changes while stopping unused upstream work.

subtopics.title: SharedFlow Replay & Overflow
subtopics.description: SharedFlow broadcasts values. Configure replay, extra buffer capacity, and overflow based on whether late or slow subscribers may miss values.

callouts.title: No Subscribers
callouts.text: With replay = 0, values emitted while nobody is subscribed are not retained. If delivery must survive absence, persist state or use a durable queue rather than treating SharedFlow as one.

sections.title: Lifecycle-Aware Android Collection
sections.description: Tie collectors to screen visibility and keep ownership explicit.

subtopics.title: Views: repeatOnLifecycle
subtopics.description: repeatOnLifecycle launches the block when the Lifecycle reaches the target state and cancels it below that state.

callouts.title: Use viewLifecycleOwner in Fragments
callouts.text: A Fragment can outlive its destroyed View. Bind UI collectors to viewLifecycleOwner to avoid touching stale bindings.

callouts.title: Parallel Collection Needs Children
callouts.text: collect never returns for an ongoing stream. Launch each independently collected Flow in its own child coroutine inside repeatOnLifecycle.

subtopics.title: Compose: collectAsStateWithLifecycle
subtopics.description: Convert a Flow or StateFlow into Compose State using Android lifecycle awareness.

callouts.title: Keep Reusable UI Platform-Neutral
callouts.text: Collect at the screen boundary and pass plain values and callbacks to reusable composables. This improves previews, testing, and reuse.

subtopics.title: Room, Paging & Database Invalidation
subtopics.description: Room query Flows re-run when observed tables are invalidated. Use Paging when datasets are too large to load and transform as one in-memory list.

tabs.label: Room Flow
Paging
tabs.code:
val pagingData: Flow<PagingData<Article>> = Pager(
    config = PagingConfig(pageSize = 30),
    pagingSourceFactory = dao::pagingSource
).flow.cachedIn(viewModelScope)

callouts.title: Transactions Define Consistency
callouts.text: A Flow makes updates observable; it does not make multi-table reads or writes atomic. Use Room transactions for invariants and map database models outside the UI.

sections.title: Testing, Debugging & Production Checklist
sections.description: Test deterministic behavior and diagnose lifetime, cancellation, and duplicate-work bugs.

subtopics.title: Test Finite & Infinite Flows
subtopics.description: Use runTest, finite terminal operators, or a background collector. Test state values rather than implementation timing whenever possible.

callouts.title: Dedicated Testing Sheet
callouts.text: This is the Flow-specific quick reference. See Android Testing for dispatcher replacement, scheduler control, fakes, Turbine-style assertions, and instrumented tests.

subtopics.title: Production Review Checklist
subtopics.description: Check semantics, ownership, cancellation, thread usage, and loss behavior before shipping.

codeBlocks.code:
□ Cold versus hot behavior is intentional
□ Hot Flow scope matches the resource lifetime
□ Mutable state is private; exposed type is immutable
□ UI state cannot represent contradictory conditions
□ UI collection is lifecycle-aware
□ Large datasets use paging instead of whole-list loading
□ Database invariants use transactions, not observation alone
□ Blocking work is main-safe and injected for tests
□ Latest/conflation/drop behavior cannot lose required work
□ Callback listeners unregister in awaitClose
□ CancellationException is not swallowed
□ retry is bounded and limited to retryable failures
□ combine inputs have sensible initial emissions
□ State values are immutable and equality behaves correctly
□ Infinite streams have deterministic tests
